title: Measurement of Claude 4.7 tokenizer costs highlights per-language token inflation
summary: HN discussion of a measurement study of Claude 4.7's new tokenizer costs; the same article was submitted separately under the title 'Claude Opus 4.7's new tokenizer: 1.47x on English, 1.01x on Chinese', indicating token-cost ratios that differ by language.

title: Multilingual LLM guardrails questioned in a widely discussed essay
source_title: Don't Trust the Salt: AI Summarization, Multilingual Safety, and LLM Guardrails
summary: Substack essay on AI summarization, multilingual safety and LLM guardrails, framed as a warning against trusting multilingual safety evaluations; the HN thread drew 225 points and 88 comments.

title: Popular video walkthrough builds a GPT tokenizer from scratch
summary: Widely discussed video that walks through building a GPT tokenizer; tokenizer construction is the mechanism behind script handling and uneven per-language tokenization in language models.

title: Multilingual guardrail evaluation for a humanitarian LLM deployment
source_title: Evaluating Multilingual, Context-Aware Guardrails: A Humanitarian LLM Use Case
summary: Mozilla.ai blog post evaluating multilingual, context-aware guardrails in a humanitarian LLM use case, a setting where safety behaviour must hold across languages rather than only in English.

title: Industry study tests eight LLMs in eight non-English languages
source_title: How well do LLMs work outside English? We tested 8 models in 8 languages [pdf]
summary: Reported benchmark study (PDF) that tested eight LLMs across eight languages to assess performance outside English; submitted to HN as a cross-lingual capability check.

title: Byte-level tokenizers favour high-resource languages and Latin script
source_title: Equity with Efficiency: An Empirical Study of Tokenizers for Multilingual Large Language Models
quote: State-of-the-art multilingual LLMs often use Byte-level Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizers that structurally favor high-resource languages and Latin scripts.
summary: Systematic comparison of equitable tokenizers across 11 Southeast Asian languages; standard byte-level BPE tokenizers structurally favour high-resource languages and Latin scripts, inflating inference cost and widening cross-lingual capability gaps.

title: Multilingual LLMs underperform smaller fine-tuned models on code-switched text
source_title: Multilingual Large Language Models Are Not (Yet) Code-Switchers
quote: current "multilingualism" in LLMs does not inherently imply proficiency with code-switching texts
summary: Empirical analysis of multilingual LLMs across sentiment analysis, machine translation, summarization and word-level language identification finds that strong zero/few-shot monolingual results do not transfer to code-switching, where much smaller fine-tuned models still win.

title: Tokenizer matters more than shared script for transfer to an unseen script
source_title: Unknown Script: Impact of Script on Cross-Lingual Transfer
quote: the importance of the tokenizer as a stronger factor than the shared script, language similarity, and model size
summary: Experiments with monolingual and multilingual models pre-trained under different tokenization schemes, transferring to a language whose script is absent from pre-training; the tokenizer was a stronger factor than shared script, language similarity and model size.

title: Higher overall multilingual accuracy does not imply fairer cross-language results
source_title: Quantifying Language Disparities in Multilingual Large Language Models
quote: higher overall model performance does not necessarily imply greater fairness across languages
summary: Proposes a framework with three interpretable metrics that disentangles confounded multilingual evaluations; a case study of 13 model variants on 11 multilingual datasets finds that higher overall model performance does not necessarily imply greater fairness across languages.

title: False-friend benchmark exposes high-resource bias in cross-lingual word sense
source_title: Thank You, Stingray: Multilingual Large Language Models Can Not (Yet) Disambiguate Cross-Lingual Word Sense
quote: they tend to be biased toward higher-resource languages
summary: Introduces StingrayBench, which uses false friends in four language pairs (Indonesian-Malay, Indonesian-Tagalog, Chinese-Japanese, English-German) to test cross-lingual sense disambiguation; analysis finds models biased toward higher-resource languages.
